other_failure_modes.name: Temporal leakage causing train-test feature skew
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes global aggregations over the entire dataset (e.g., player mean score across all games) and assigns them to all rows. For training data, this leaks future game outcomes into earlier games. For test data, it uses only historical data, creating a massive distribution mismatch between training and inference.

other_failure_modes.name: Incorrect temporal features on test set
other_failure_modes.description: Temporal/sequential features (like cumulative counts or time since last event) are computed on the test set in isolation. For subjects that exist in both train and test sets, their historical events in the training data are ignored, resulting in incorrect feature values during inference.

summary: The agent correctly sets up a validation split grouped by player and builds a wide array of features. However, its feature engineering suffers from severe temporal leakage by aggregating all future games into historical rows, creating a major train-test distribution skew. Additionally, it computes sequential features on the test set in isolation, uses naive equal-weight ensembling, and evaluates its stochastic models only once on a single split.
